questions.solution_text:
Change in mass $=120-40$
$=80\text{ g}$
Rate $=\dfrac{80}{8}$
$=10\text{ g/day}$, so the soap's mass is decreasing at $10$ g/day.

questions.solution_text:
Starting balance $=\$60$ (where the line meets the vertical axis).
Rate $=\dfrac{180-60}{8}$
$=15$
$=\$15$ per week.

questions.solution_text:
During the second stage the volume rises from $18$ L to $58$ L over $10$ minutes.
Rate $=\dfrac{58-18}{16-6}$
$=\dfrac{40}{10}$
$=4\text{ L/min}$

options.why: read the more steeply decreasing line as the slower-burning candle
compared the two candles' heights at $10$ hours instead of comparing their rates
gave candle Q's rate alone instead of the difference between the two rates

questions.solution_text:
Candle P: rate $=\dfrac{20-10}{10}=1\text{ cm/h}$
Candle Q: rate $=\dfrac{20-4}{10}=1.6\text{ cm/h}$
Candle Q burns faster, by $1.6-1=0.6\text{ cm/h}$.

options.why: added the full $12$ years of growth on top of the height already reached at year $5$, double-counting the first $5$ years
multiplied the rate by $12$ but forgot to add the tree's starting height
read the height shown at year $5$ as if it were already the height at year $12$

questions.solution_text:
Rate $=\dfrac{145-120}{5-0}$
$=5\text{ cm/year}$
Height after $12$ years $=120+5\times12$
$=180\text{ cm}$

questions.solution_text:
The paused stage (from $6$ to $10$ minutes) has zero rate and cannot be used for the final stage.
From $10$ minutes ($80$°C) to $18$ minutes ($92$°C):
Rate $=\dfrac{92-80}{18-10}$
$=\dfrac{12}{8}$
$=1.5$°C/min

questions.solution_text:
Sprinkler 1: rate $=\dfrac{25}{5}=5\text{ L/min}$
Sprinkler 2: $180\text{ L/h}\div60=3\text{ L/min}$
Sprinkler 3: $90\text{ mL/s}\times60=5400\text{ mL/min}=5.4\text{ L/min}$
Sprinkler 3 uses water fastest, at $5.4$ L/min.
